GANGTOK: Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang on Saturday announced the launch of the CM-SAATHI initiative to provide free, high-quality coaching for JEE and NEET aspirants from poor socio-economic backgrounds.Speaking at a function on the occasion of Teachers' Day here, he said the scheme was launched in collaboration with IIT Kanpur, under which students from poor families will be given a two-month crash course to prepare for the engineering and medical entrance tests.Tamang said that the proposal in this regard was approved by the state cabinet yesterday."There are many students from poor backgrounds who aspire to compete for JEE and NEET, but they can't afford the cost of proper coaching centres," the chief minister said.Tamang, himself a former teacher before entering politics more than three decades ago, paid tribute to the teachers and appreciated their dedication, sacrifices and challenges."Their unwavering faith in education continues to inspire us, and today's teachers are the proud custodians of that legacy of sacrifice, service and dedication," he said.Tamang said that his government has always treated education not as an expenditure, but as the most important investment."With approximately 15 per cent of the state's total expenditure invested in education during 2025-26, we remain firmly committed to our vision of making Sikkim an education hub and building a Sunaulo, Samriddha ani Saamarth (Golden, Prosperous, and Capable) Sikkim," he said.It is a matter of great pride that Sikkim was declared a Fully Literate State on 27 May 2026, which marked an important milestone in the state's educational journey.The CM said that his government has made continued efforts to strengthen the education system through teacher regularisation and recruitment, and various schemes.Tamang said that the state government is working towards introducing the Sikkim Life Skills Curriculum, which will equip students with practical skills such as CPR, first aid, fire safety and disaster preparedness."As a Himalayan State situated in a high seismic-risk zone, I emphasised that disaster preparedness is not an option but a necessity. Our objective is to create a generation capable of saving not only their own lives but also the lives of others," he said.Observing that Sikkim has developed adequate education-related infrastructure, he said that by 2035, students from Sikkim would not have to leave the state in search of quality education."Instead, we want students from across India to come to Sikkim in search of excellent, inclusive and future-ready education," Tamang added.
Article Summary: Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang announced the launch of the CM-SAATHI initiative to provide free, high-quality coaching for JEE and NEET aspirants. The scheme was launched in collaboration with IIT Kanpur, under which students from poor families will be given a two-month crash course.

Article Title: Kenney, Sikh leader share dais as Mohan Bhagwat makes global Hindu call
Article Text:
Mohan Bhagwat outlines Hinduism’s global role during Canada visit (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A day after telling a New York audience that a Hindu who wanted Muslims excluded from India could not remain a Hindu, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat Monday used his first visit to Canada to cast Hindus as builders of an “exemplary society” worldwide and India as a “vishwaguru” serving humanity, not a “mahashakti” seeking dominance.The speeches shared themes of oneness, but differed in emphasis. In New York, amid protests and criticism of RSS, Bhagwat addressed concerns about exclusion; in Toronto, he explained how Hindu society should organise and lead internationally without imposing its beliefs.“The word Hindu cannot be defined by any specific language, through any specific worship or through any living style,” he said. The dais reflected that wider outreach: former Alberta premier and federal cabinet minister Jason Kenney and Kashmir Singh Dhaliwal of the Khalsa Diwan Society joined Bhagwat, placing a senior Canadian political figure and a representative of a Sikh institution alongside the RSS chief at a gathering opposed by sections of the South Asian community.“We have to build our society in every country, all over the world, which is an exemplary society for the world,” Bhagwat said at the “Hindu Vishwa Bandhu — Embrace the World in Friendship” event. The programme in Vaughan, in the Greater Toronto Area, was organised by Canadian Hindus for Outreach, Relations and Dialogue.Presenting India’s global role as one based on service rather than power, Bhagwat said: “It became ‘vishwaguru’, not ‘mahashakti’.”Whenever help had been sought during an international crisis, he said, India had not refused. “This is the tradition. This is the DNA of Bharat.”Bhagwat said the RSS organised Hindus “exactly for this purpose — and nothing else”, describing the purpose as developing individuals who would dedicate themselves to serving humanity.The RSS chief coupled the call for organisation with a message on civic responsibility. People connected with India but settled elsewhere, he said, “have to be honest, contributing citizens of that country”. At the same time, they should take to the world an outlook in which individuals, society and the environment could progress without harming one another.He said this should be done through conduct rather than imposition. “We don’t force,” Bhagwat said. “We are the leaders who lead from within and lead by example.” He added: “Hindus respect all. Hindus accept all.”Going beyond the familiar expression “unity in diversity”, Bhagwat said Hindu tradition also recognised “diversities of unity”. Different identities, he argued, were expressions of an underlying oneness. “Diversity is never a problem for unity,” he said. “All the diversities are expressions of unity.”Bhagwat’s visit came despite demands from New Democratic Party and civil-society groups that he be denied entry to Canada. The venue was disclosed shortly before the programme amid security concerns.
Article Summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat uses first visit to Canada to cast Hindus as builders of an ‘exemplary society’ worldwide. He says India is a ‘vishwaguru’ serving humanity, not a “mahashakti’ seeking dominance.

Article Title: Output overdrive: 30% productivity boost could power 35% of future manufacturing
Article Text:
30% productivity boost could power 35% of future manufacturing

Small factories lag larger firms

Six ways to drive manufacturing growth

Productivity

Workforce shifts

Global integration

Investment in capacity

Innovation and technology

Consumption-led growth.

India's manufacturing sector could get nearly 35 per cent of its future output simply by getting its workforce 30 per cent more productive.The finding comes from KPMG's analysis of more than 130 large Indian manufacturing companies over 10 years. It found that companies which improved productivity faster than their peers also saw stronger growth in profits and market value.Their net profits grew by around 10-11 per cent annually, compared with about 7 per cent for companies with average productivity.The difference was even wider in market value. Companies leading in productivity recorded around 19 per cent CAGR in market capitalisation, against nearly 10 per cent for average-productivity organisations.Overall, productivity-leading companies saw more than 50 per cent higher profitability growth and twice the market-cap expansion compared with their peers.The gains, however, are not spread evenly across the manufacturing sector.More than 70 per cent of large manufacturing companies would need transformative measures to achieve the productivity growth rate required for India's manufacturing ambition, the report said.There is also a wide gap between smaller and larger factories. Small and unorganised manufacturing facilities produce less than 20 per cent of the output per worker compared with large firms.Even among companies within the manufacturing sector, productivity can vary sharply, with differences ranging between 300 per cent and 1,000 per cent.KPMG identified six broad levers for manufacturing growth:But productivity stands out because its benefits can continue over time.“Productivity is Indian manufacturing's most powerful growth lever,” the report said, adding that productivity gains “embed permanently into the system, raising output, margins, and competitiveness year after year.”“Unlike scale or demand-led levers, productivity improvements embed permanently into the system,” the report said.The report said improving productivity would require companies to rethink how work is organised, how organisations are structured and how their workforce is deployed.Digital and AI tools, performance management and changes in workplace culture would also be needed to support these changes, it said.
Article Summary: India's manufacturing sector could get nearly 35 per cent of its future output simply by getting its workforce 30 per cent more productive. The finding comes from KPMG's analysis of more than 130 large Indian manufacturing companies over 10 years. Small and unorganised manufacturing facilities produce less than 20% of the output per worker compared with large firms.

Article Title: Census 2027: The 14 questions and why opposition fears an NPR 'backdoor'
Article Text:
Opposition is raising questions over the methodology of population enumeration, alleging that it too has a “deeper nefarious purpose”

What is the controversy?

What are the opposition's charges

Difference between Census and NPR

What the law says

Can Census data be shared?

Census data must remain a statistical instrument and “not become a backdoor for state surveillance”.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Although six years late, enumerators have started knocking on doors for the decennial headcount in Ladakh and snowbound regions such as Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand starting September 1.But doubts and fears have preceded the Census, turning what was meant to be a routine exercise to track population growth and aid policy planning into a fresh political flashpoint.Until now, the caste census had been the main point of contention between the opposition and the government. The opposition had questioned the intent and methodology of an exercise being conducted in the country after almost 100 years.The contention has now moved beyond the caste census, and the opposition is also raising questions over the methodology of population enumeration, alleging that it too has a “deeper nefarious purpose”.On August 14, the Centre notified the list of questions that officials will ask during population enumeration. The questionnaire, however, contains 14 new or modified questions compared with the 2011 Census.These include spouse's name, nationality as declared, father's particulars, mother's particulars, SC/ST/caste, literacy and digital literacy, highest educational level attained and stream/discipline, place of Covid-19 vaccination, total number of bank accounts, mobile number, Aadhaar number, voter ID number, passport number for Indian passport holders, and availability of a driving licence.Interestingly, several of these questions, including details of a person's father and mother and their places of birth, were also part of the National Population Register (NPR) schedule notified in 2020.Moreover, the Union Budget presented on February 1 this year allocated Rs 6,000 crore for the NPR and Census 2027, even though the government has not yet notified any schedule for the NPR.The Budget document said the allocation included provisions for the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India and various schemes of the Registrar General of India, with Rs 6,000 crore earmarked for NPR and Census 2027.Following the notification of the questionnaire, the opposition has accused the Centre of turning the Census exercise into a “backdoor for the NPR, and eventually, NRC”.Congress Rajya Sabha member Jairam Ramesh said the methodology of asking questions in Census 2027 is flawed and alleged that questions on religion, date of birth, place of birth and parents' details had never been asked in previous enumerations.“Census is confidential. Clearly, Census 27 has a deeper nefarious purpose,” he said in a post on X.Similarly, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee alleged that the Centre was planning to conduct the Census in the form of NPR.“They have started the census. Census in the form of NPR. You have to provide your bank account number, mobile number and Aadhaar number. You must disclose the full details of all family members,” Mamata said.“No political party has been informed. At least the Trinamool Congress was not informed. Nobody knows whose name will be deleted. Is it going to be another SIR? Who knows,” she added.Even during the run-up to the Bengal assembly elections, she alleged that the Centre was planning to 'take away' people's citizenship in the name of NRC.Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan also raised questions over the inclusion of the new questions, arguing that the Census should not be used to divide people.“The reported inclusion of questions about parents’ place of birth and religion in the upcoming Census is deeply troubling. The Census must not become a backdoor for the NPR and, eventually, the NRC. Citizenship cannot be tied to religion, and no census should be used to divide our people. The Union Government must immediately drop such divisive questions. Secular forces must stand united against this dangerous move,” Vijayan said.Census and NPR differ in their legal basis, objectives and the nature of information they are designed to collect.The Census is a statistical exercise meant to produce data on population, literacy, occupation, migration, housing and, in 2027, caste. It is used for making policies, allocating resources and delimitation.On the other hand, the National Population Register is a continuously updated register of “usual residents” created under the Citizenship Act, 1955.It is designed to maintain an identifiable database of people who have lived in a locality for at least six months or intend to stay there for the next six months, irrespective of their citizenship.The NPR collects detailed identity information, including names, parents' particulars, place of birth, nationality as declared, address and identity documents such as Aadhaar, voter ID and passport, as well as mobile numbers. The data collected through NPR is linked to the proposed National Register of Citizens.Under Rule 3 of the Citizenship Rules, the Centre may order preparation of the National Population Register, from which the Local Register of citizens is prepared after verification.Rule 4 provides that individuals whose citizenship is doubtful can be flagged in the Population Register for further enquiry.The NPR data was first collected in 2010 alongside the 2011 Census house-listing exercise and updated through a door-to-door survey in 2015.However, both the Census and NPR are conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.The inclusion of the new questions has raised a larger question: Can information collected during the Census be accessed or used by government agencies for purposes beyond the exercise itself?The law says no. Section 15 of the Census Act, 1948 provides a strong legal shield around personal information collected during the Census.“No person shall have a right to inspect any book, register or record made by a census-officer in the discharge of his duty,” the Act says.“No entry in any such book, register, record or schedule shall be admissible as evidence in any civil proceeding whatsoever or in any criminal proceeding other than a prosecution under this Act or any other law for any act or omission which constitutes an offence under this Act,” it further says.This means that the information collected through the census cannot be used by other government agencies to determine the citizenship of a person.Speaking to The Times of India, advocate Ajinkya Udane said it would therefore be incorrect to accuse the government of divulging information collected through the Census.“Through the census, private information of people is being asked. However, the Census Act bars the government from divulging this information to its agencies,” Udane said.“So, to accuse the government of doing something which the law bars it from doing is not correct,” he added.Cyber and privacy law expert advocate Prashant Mali, however, stressed that Census data must remain a statistical instrument and “not become a backdoor for state surveillance”.“Section 15 of the Census Act creates a strong statutory confidentiality barrier. Individual census records are not open to inspection and are not admissible as evidence. Therefore, census information cannot legitimately be converted into an evidentiary database for citizenship determination merely because another government authority wants to use it,” Mali said.He said that even if a census record, or personal information traceable back to it, is accessed or used in a manner prohibited by Section 15, describing it as “independent intelligence” would not cure the underlying violation.“Substance must prevail over form. If the underlying census record or identifiable information has been accessed or used contrary to Section 15, I feel calling it independent intelligence does not cure the problem,” he said.“I feel the State cannot do indirectly through a citizenship inquiry what Section 15 of the Census Act prohibits it from doing directly through the Census record. A lawful purpose for processing does not automatically create a lawful source of data,” he told The Times of India.During the conversation, Mali said that the interaction between the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) and the Census Act will also be interesting to watch during the exercise.“DPDPA (Digital Personal Data Protection Act) Sections 3–17 are scheduled to come into force 18 months after 13 November 2025, i.e. 13 May 2027, while Census 2027 field operations occur around that period,” Mali said.“This makes the interaction between the Census Act and DPDPA particularly interesting for the 2027 exercise,” he added.The Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) is primary law which will dictate how the personal data is collected, processed and stored.It sets out obligations for entities handling personal data - such as obtaining consent, limiting use to the stated purpose, and ensuring data security - and grants individuals rights over their own data, including access and correction.
Article Summary: Census data must remain a statistical instrument and “not become a backdoor for state surveillance’ Opposition is raising questions over the methodology of population enumeration, alleging that it too has a “deeper nefarious purpose” The questionnaire, however, contains 14 new or modified questions compared with the 2011 Census.

Article Title: No registration number, no attendance: NMC warns medical colleges
Article Text:
Medical colleges have one month to update faculty registration numbers on the attendance system. Failure to comply will result in blocked daily attendance for specified teaching staff. The National Medical Commission issued this warning after finding blank registration fields. Colleges must review and update all medical faculty and resident profiles accurately. Non-medical faculty will have 'NA' entered in the registration number field.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Medical colleges have one month to update the National Medical Register (NMR) or State Medical Register (SMR) numbers of their faculty and specified teaching staff on the Aadhaar Enabled Biometric Attendance System (AEBAS), failing which their daily attendance could be blocked and automatically rejected.The National Medical Commission (NMC) has warned that this may adversely impact the compliance status of the medical college during NMC assessments and inspections.The warning was issued on September 3 after the NMC found that nodal officers at several medical colleges had left the NMR or SMR registration-number field blank while registering faculty on the attendance portal.The commission has directed colleges to review and update the profiles of all medical faculty, Junior Residents, Senior Residents, tutors and demonstrators with correct and valid NMR or SMR numbers.For non-medical faculty and tutors or demonstrators holding Master of Science (MSc) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) qualifications, colleges have been instructed to enter “NA” in the registration-number field.The NMC has made it clear that leaving the registration-number field blank will not be permitted.The directive effectively makes faculty registration details part of the attendance compliance process, rather than a routine profile correction.The memorandum has been sent to deans, principals and directors of all medical colleges and institutions, besides state and Union Territory medical education departments, directorates of medical education and State Medical Councils.The move is under the provisions of the Undergraduate and Postgraduate Minimum Standard Requirements and Medical Assessment and Rating Board regulations, which provide for periodic, transparent and digitally verified assessment of teaching staff in medical institutions.
Article Summary: Medical colleges have one month to update faculty registration numbers on the attendance system. Failure to comply will result in blocked daily attendance for specified teaching staff. The National Medical Commission issued this warning after finding blank registration fields. Non-medical faculty will have 'NA' entered in the registration number field.

Article Title: 'Some calling for tariff barriers to go up arbitrarily without economic logic': Belgian PM takes veiled dig at Trump
Article Text:
Belgian PM Bart De Wever took a veiled dig at Trump’s tariff policy, saying barriers were being imposed “arbitrarily” and without economic logic.

Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever took a veiled dig at US President Donald Trump over his decision to impose tariffs saying many voices are now calling for tariff barriers to go up but they do it arbitrarily. De Wever said the India-European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement (FTA) made both sides resilient against disruption and coercion. “Ladies and gentlemen, more and more voices today are calling for barriers to go up, for markets to be shut off, for tariffs to be imposed. Some do this entirely arbitrarily. They decide something on Monday, they revoke it on Wednesday and reinstall on Saturday. You all know who I am talking about. I am not going to say the name but you know these people arbitrarily do it without any economic logic at all,” De Wever said without naming Trump. Wever was in Mumbai for the India–Belgium High-Level Dialogue on the India–EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA). Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the India-EU FTA was a win-win for everyone. CM Devendra Fadnavis said India EU FTA will fundamentally change the India EU relationship Maharashtra should become the demonstrative state for the India EU FTA implementation.Wever said PM Narendra Modi is a wise leader, and one of the most inspiring world leaders. “Antwerp is pocket sized Mumbai in Belgium. We are sailing through rough waters but India and the EU have chosen partnership. We have concluded the mother of all deals. It is an expression of mutual respect. Our cooperation is directed towards international order. The FTA arrives at a critical moment. To make trading partnerships more predictable. If every community in Belgium is like the Indian community I would be a happy Prime Minister,” De Wever said.Goyal said the India EU FTA was in the making for 25 years. “It is a win-win agreement, it will open opportunities for farmers, start ups, women entrepreneurs, it has something for everyone. It’s been deftly negotiated protecting sensitive sectors on both sides. It offers huge potential for both sides," Goyal said.“66% India’s data center capacity is in Maharashtra. We want Belgium to be part of Maharashtra’s journey to a trillion dollar economy. We have bilateral trade of 13.8 billion USD. But it understates the potential. Maharashtra would like to contribute and be the principal engine of this growth story. I want to make a direct invitation. If Belgium companies are looking at India for investment after the FTA, look and come to Maharashtra. We have a manufacturing ecosystem. This should become a template for Belgium - Maharashtra partnerships,” Fadnavis said.Fadnavis said Maharashtra would like to be the first state to translate the FTA into action. “Belgium Maharashtra projects must be fast tracked. If Belgium companies identifies - project, we will dedicate a team and work with Belgium to make it happen. Come to Maharashtra and from Maharashtra serve India and the world.Maharashtra is volunteering to convert strategic direction into action,” Fadnavis said.De Wever is on an official visit to India from 2-4 September. This is De Wever's first visit to India since taking office in February 2025. On Thursday, De Wever began his visit by paying homage to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat. De Wever then held bilateral talks with the PM Narendra Modi.
Article Summary: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever took a veiled dig at US President Donald Trump over his decision to impose tariffs. He said many voices are now calling for tariff barriers to go up but they do it arbitrarily. Wever said the India- European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement (FTA) made both sides resilient against disruption and coercion.

Article Title: UN approves resolution to declare Nov 27 as ‘International Day For Elimination Of Child, Early & Forced Marriage’
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a significant development that brings focus on the need to step up action to deliver on the Sustainable Development Goals 2030, the United Nations (UN) has declared November 27 the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. The date carries special significance for India, which backed the resolution steered by Sierra Leone, as it was on Nov 27 that the govt had launched the ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat’ campaign in 2024.Even though underage marriage has been declining over the decades, the numbers are still a concern calling for greater efforts to eradicate the problem. According to the 2019-21 National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 23.3% of women aged 20-24 were married before the age of 18. This came down to 20.1% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).Just Rights for Children founder Bhuwan Ribhu, who has been vociferously advocating for a dedicated day and has worked closely with the drafting of the resolution, said that the announcement is very significant for India as it is an opportunity to lead by example and meet the elimination targets.Welcoming the UN approval for the demand from countries across the world, Ribhu said, “Today marks the tipping point, showing that the end of the crime of child marriage is inevitable and imminent.Now is the time for governments globally to provide decisive leadership to end child marriage by 2030 and ensure education, protection and development of every child to realise their full potential. I am grateful to the First Lady of Sierra Leone for her leadership in championing this cause and would also like to thank the countries that co-sponsored our resolution. “ He was present at the UN as the civil society representative when the UN approved the resolution.“The Government of India has set a target of reducing the prevalence of child marriage by 10% by 2026. With continued efforts at the national and state levels, the prevalence of child marriage in India is expected to fall below 15% by the end of 2026. The global commitment to eliminate child marriage by 2030 is aligned with target 5.3 of Sustainable Development Goal 5 (Gender Equality), which calls for the elimination of all harmful practices, including child, early, and forced marriage,” Ribhu added.He shared that plans are afoot to hold extensive outreach campaigns in coordination with the govt and states ahead of November 27 to ensure that the day becomes a space to dwell on progress made and the way forward and does not end up as a symbolic reminder of the problem.
Article Summary: The UN has declared November 27 the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. The date carries special significance for India, which backed the resolution steered by Sierra Leone. It was on Nov 27 that the govt had launched the ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat’ campaign.

Article Title: ‘Will be compelled to launch large-scale agitation’: Sonam Wangchuk ahead of Ladakh talks with Centre
Article Text:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk (PTI photo)

NEW DELHI: Ladakh-based activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday said the Leh Apex Body (LAB) would be compelled to launch a “very large-scale agitation” if the Union government fails to make “concrete” progress on the group’s key demands.“If stepmotherly treatment is meted out to Ladakh and the people living along the borders, then we will be compelled to launch a very large-scale agitation after September 9,” PTI quoted him as saying. He was referring to the date when an LAB sub-committee is scheduled to meet Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) officials in Delhi to press for its demands.Wangchuk further announced that the outfit's proposed march from Kargil to Leh, scheduled to begin on September 10, had been postponed in view of the MHA talks. However, he warned the march would be revived if the talks fail to produce a “satisfactory” outcome.“We have collectively decided to postpone the 'padyatra' for the time being. We will once again appeal to people from across India to come forward in support of Ladakh, in support of the environment, and in support of the people of Ladakh who remain steadfast on the country's borders,” he stated.He added that the LAB is observing September as “Martyrs' Month” in memory of those killed, injured and jailed last year.The activist was referring to the violence in Leh, the Union territory's capital, on September 24 last year, during which four civilians were killed, allegedly in police firing. Wangchuk himself was detained under the stringent National Security Act and released six months later, in March this year.Wangchuk, who emerged as the face of the recent student protests in Delhi and sat on a hunger strike for more than 20 days, also said the LAB expects the Centre to bring a detailed draft on the proposed Ladakh assembly, including its powers and rights, to the September 9 meeting.The outfit has been demanding legislation for Ladakh at the Union territory level, safeguards under Article 371, withdrawal of cases filed after the September 24 violence last year, compensation for victims and publication of the inquiry commission report. The LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) have been jointly spearheading the agitation since Ladakh was granted Union territory status in August 2019 and have held several rounds of talks with the Centre since 2021.
Article Summary: Ladakh-based activist Sonam Wangchuk said the Leh Apex Body (LAB) would be compelled to launch a “very large-scale agitation” if the Union government fails to make “concrete” progress on the group’s key demands. He was referring to the violence in Leh, the Union territory's capital, on September 24 last year.
